# rawmktg

> rawmktg is a blog covering B2B marketing strategy, SEO, GEO (Generative Engine Optimization), AI search visibility, and content marketing for SaaS companies.

## Published Posts

- [The rawmktg Measurement Methodology](https://rawmktg.com/methodology) - The canonical, versioned standard behind every visibility figure rawmktg publishes. Prompt portfolio tiers (baseline 50-150, decision-grade 250-500, enterprise 500+); a fixed 8 to 12 runs per prompt per engine (default 10) at every tier; per-engine reporting with evidence-based weights; 95% Wilson intervals and response-level bootstrap; a 200-observation per brand-engine cell reporting floor; monthly cadence on a frozen versioned portfolio; and a decision-grade vs directional labelling rule. Version 1.0, effective 26 August 2026, with a changelog.
- [Digital PR and Data Studies: The Link Play AI Cites](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/mentions-beat-links) - August 2026. The off-site authority layer for AI search. Your owned domain is only 5-10% of the source citations in AI answers (McKinsey); the rest is earned editorial, review platforms, aggregators and community you do not control, and ~82% of AI citations trace to earned editorial media (Muck Rack). Mentions beat links: an Ahrefs analysis of ~75,000 brands puts web-wide brand mention frequency at 0.664 Spearman correlation with AI citation inclusion vs 0.204 for backlinks (~3x the signal); links still drive crawler discovery but are no longer the dominant term, and Google-organic vs AI-cited overlap collapsed from ~70% to under 20% (83% of AI Overview citations sit outside the organic top ten). The GEO experiment (Princeton/Georgia Tech/AI2/IIT Delhi, SIGKDD 2024) tested 9 modifications on a 10,000-query benchmark: attributed quotations +41% and precise statistics +31% are the top position-adjusted-word-count levers, keyword stuffing is -8%; strategies stack with heavy overlap (model ~50%, not 85%); when all sources optimise, visibility redistributes to challengers (rank 5 +115.1%, rank 1 -30.3%). The highest-yield PR asset is an original data study because it natively produces both top levers; +239% median citation lift from syndicated research. Four archetypes (survey, internal telemetry, index/benchmark, meta-analysis); telemetry is nearly free and unreplicable. Design in stat units (precise number + named methodology + attributed quote in a sub-45-word block); citable stat density should clear 4 per 1,000 words; write the headline before the survey; publish the raw dataset. Distribution is concentrated: top 15 domains hold ~68% of AI citations (5WPR, 680M citations), so 30 placements in retrieved domains beat 300 in the long tail; entity corroboration index log-weights independent domains (two domains beat four mentions on one); sequence an exclusive first. The unlinked mention is near-complete for retrieval, track mention volume per domain, not links. Package the hub front-loaded (44.2% of citations from the first 30%), deep (>20k chars = ~4.3x citations) and modular, with Article+Dataset+Organization JSON-LD (~45% higher citation rates; Wikidata explains up to 49.9% of B2B recommendation variance); allow OAI-SearchBot, not just GPTBot. Measure brand mention share over many runs (5 min, 10 better); the cited domains are your outreach list. Report the citation lag (mentions lead, citations lag) and the Dark AI gap (70.6% referrer-stripped, dark sessions convert at 10.21% vs 2.46% baseline). Includes a 90-day sequence, 6 formulas (stacked lift, citable stat density, entity corroboration index, brand mention share, hidden dark-AI revenue, cost per citation point) and working YAML/Python/JSON-LD/robots code.
- [The Broken-Sitemap Tax: XML Sitemaps for AI Discovery](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/xml-sitemaps-for-ai-discovery) - August 2026. The discovery layer for AI search: your XML sitemap is now a scheduling instruction, not an inventory manifest. Three crawler families read it differently: training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot) ingest a bulk manifest patiently and tolerate ~5 hops; real-time search indexers (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) read lastmod to prioritise the recrawl queue, ignore Crawl-delay, and enforce a hard 1-3 redirect-hop ceiling vs Googlebot's ~10 and the spec's 30; user-triggered fetchers arrive with a URL and ignore the file. The three-hop ceiling: scheme + host + trailing-slash normalisation can burn the whole budget before content is served, and the crawler abandons the request silently (a 301 in your log, then nothing). discovery_yield = share of declared URLs that return 200, resolve inside the hop budget, and self-canonical; most sites score 0.60-0.85. Status codes are cache instructions: 301/308 cache the target (pay the hop once), 302/307 do not (re-requested every cycle); the 301-then-302 pattern invalidates the cache; redirect-to-noindex wastes the whole fetch. Root files (robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, llms-full.txt) must return 200 with zero client-visible hops, PerplexityBot refuses any redirect on llms.txt, use a transparent internal rewrite not a redirect. lastmod is the signal you probably lie with: build-stamping today's date on all 12,000 URLs earns a recrawl demotion; timestamp_trust = content-changed URLs / lastmod-changed URLs (below 0.2, publish no lastmod). Fix with hash-based lastmod (hash the rendered body minus volatile regions). Partition sitemaps under ~5,000 URLs with a sitemap index; drop changefreq and priority (ignored). Freshness is the highest-leverage lever: pages updated within 30 days are cited ~3.2x more, 76.4% of top ChatGPT Search citations come from pages under 30 days, citation half-life ~2 months; AI Overviews is more forgiving (65% within a year). IndexNow inverts pull to push: notify Bing, Yandex, Naver, Seznam, Yep on change, recrawl in seconds not days, ~10s signed fanout; verify a root key file, submit only changed URLs. What a clean sitemap can't do: get you cited, that is content (quotations +41%, statistics +31-41%, cited sources +28% and +115% at rank 5, strict headings +17.3%, keyword stuffing -8%); and selection differs from absorption (ChatGPT 6.88 citations / 0.2713 influence, AI Overviews 12.06 / 0.0584, Perplexity 16.35 / 0.0646). Put a number on it: the tax (redirect hops x fetches, x egress) and a Sitemap Health Index (0.40 response + 0.30 hop + 0.20 timestamp trust + 0.10 freshness), gate both in CI. A 90-day sequence: routing first, timestamps second, partition and push third, telemetry last. Includes working bash/nginx/python/xml/yaml (hop sweep, transparent rewrites, hash-based lastmod, async validator, IndexNow pipeline, GitHub Actions discovery-gate).
- [Do AI Crawlers Render JavaScript?](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/do-ai-crawlers-render-javascript) - August 2026. A rendering/SSR teardown of 12 AI crawlers. Roughly 69% of AI crawlers cannot execute JavaScript; in a 12-crawler test 9 ran no runtime at all (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Meta-ExternalAgent, Bytespider, CCBot all FAIL), 2 pass only because they inherit a search render pipeline (Google-Extended via Googlebot WRS, Applebot browser-based), Bingbot is LIMITED. Crawling vs asset-fetching vs script-execution are three different operations; fetching a .js file is not executing it (ClaudeBot fetches JS on ~23.84% of requests, runs none; 500M+ GPTBot fetches showed zero client-side execution). The user agents advertise Chrome but are HTTP clients in a costume. A client-rendered SPA returns an app shell (0 bytes extractable) while the hydrated DOM holds the pricing table. Content Visibility Ratio = raw body text / rendered body text (SSR ~1.0, CSR ~0.0); weight the site score by commercial value. The five-second live-retrieval budget (ChatGPT-User issues HTTP 499 and falls back to Bing); crawl waste (ChatGPT ~34.82% 404s from unresolved hashed asset names); the dual-invisibility trap (direct fetch empty AND ~92% Bing-index fallback empty). Ranking on Google proves nothing because Google renders in a deferred second pass and AI engines do not. Test with a raw curl + grep, a multi-bot sweep, or a CVR check in CI; do not use Search Console. Four fixes: SSR, SSG, ISR, or edge prerendering (a Cloudflare Worker serving bots a cached snapshot); plus free wins (native details/summary instead of JS accordions, mirror JSON-LD facts into semantic HTML). Fix the pages where Risk = citation share x (1 - CVR) is highest: pricing, product/specs, comparison. A 30-day sequence with a CVR floor of 0.85 in CI.
- [Share of Model: How to Actually Measure It](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/share-of-model-measurement) - August 2026. The measurement method for Share of Model, the metric that replaces the screenshot. Definition: your weighted brand presence divided by the total weighted presence of every brand in the category, over a fixed prompt portfolio, on the same engines, on a fixed cadence. Covers the naive inclusion-rate formula and why it lies (footnote = recommendation, every engine equal, every question equal -> rank inversion); the weighted formula (engine weight w_e summing to 1, intent weight 0.5x-2.0x, presence score in [0,1]); a five-dimension presence score (mention 0.30, recommendation 0.30, position 0.20, sentiment 0.15, entity accuracy 0.05); sample size (8-12 runs per prompt per engine, ~1,900 observations for a ±2-point margin at a 27% rate, a 250-500 prompt portfolio); Wilson score intervals for rates and a response-level bootstrap for the composite; why engines must be reported separately then weighted; portfolio construction (15% navigational / 35% discovery / 30% comparative / 20% transactional, versioned, 80% stable); benchmark bands by vertical (leaders 35-48%, challengers 15-32%, emerging 3-15%); ROI and cost-of-inaction formulas; a 90-day stand-up; and seven failure modes (single-run sampling, portfolio drift, blended-only reporting, alias misses, weight tinkering, under-sampled cells, denominator confusion).
- [The 'Best X for Y' Page AI Pulls Into Shortlists](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/comparison-pages-ai-shortlists) - August 2026. The comparison-page playbook for AI search. Roughly 63% of AI citations on commercial queries go to ranked "Top N" listicles; comparison pages take ~40% where relevant; vendor product pages ~10%. Only ~12% of AI-cited URLs also sit in Google's organic top 10 (6-8% on ChatGPT), so retrievability, not domain authority, is the gate. The four levers that get a page quoted: a verdict box in the first 100 words (44.2% of extracted citations come from the first 30% of a page), one verifiable fact per 100 words, H2s phrased as the buyer's question (41% vs 29% citation rate), and neutrality (naming where a competitor wins; outbound citations lift citation odds +115.1% for low-authority domains). Plus nested ItemList + SoftwareApplication + FAQPage schema, a before/after page rebuild, how to choose "best X for Y" segments from evidence, prompt-repository measurement (BVR, SoV, AICF), and a 90-day sequence.
- [Why AI Cites Domo Over Databricks](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/why-ai-cites-domo-over-databricks) - June 2026. A GEO/SEO teardown of six data-analytics SaaS platforms (Databricks, Splunk, Domo, Alteryx, Baremetrics, Sisense). The six-stage visibility engine (access, discovery, structured data, content, authority, citation); the citation leaderboard (Splunk 1,131, Domo 1,084, Databricks 629); and the core finding: DR-70 Domo out-cites DR-88 Databricks because of GEO hygiene, a rich llms.txt vs a crawler-blocking WAF. Per-brand forensic cards, a technical-stack matrix, an eight-play playbook, and an attack plan. The unclaimed opening: pairing a definitional glossary with FAQPage schema and llms.txt.

- [Does llms.txt Actually Do Anything Yet?](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/does-llms-txt-do-anything-yet): 515M bot events, only 408 hit llms.txt. Search crawlers ignore it; coding agents (Claude Code 76% Markdown) rely on it. The log evidence + implementation playbook.

- [How Your Page Gets Retrieved](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/how-your-page-gets-retrieved): chunking & embeddings teardown. Why AI reads chunks not pages, vector drift, contextual retrieval & late chunking (-67% failures), the rerank funnel, and a writing playbook.

Three signals (mentions, citations, recommendations), the subsystems behind each, five scoring formulas with code, the Princeton and 75k-brand evidence, and a diagnostic.
- [Authority Isn't the Moat](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/authority-isnt-the-moat): carbon and ESG software SEO/GEO teardown of 10 platforms. Why authority is uniform and content is the real moat, AI citations across 7 engines, cheap buyer keywords, and the GEO playbook.

Why authority isn't traffic (DR 68 earns 332 visits), the branded-demand trap, a 651x AI-citation spread, winnable buyer keywords, and a 90-day playbook.
- [Query Fan-Out: How One Prompt Becomes Ten Searches](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/query-fan-out-how-one-prompt-becomes-ten-searches): technical deep dive on query fan-out. How AI search splits one prompt into 8-16 hidden sub-queries, the RRF (k=60) and cosine math that decides citations, and why 95% of decisive searches have zero keyword volume.
- [Why AI Cites Reddit, G2 & Analysts Over Your Website](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/why-ai-cites-reddit-g2-analysts) - June 2026. Authority-seeding playbook: AI engines are consensus engines that cross-reference third-party sources, so review sites drive up to 85% of B2B AI citations and AI-citation traffic converts ~5x higher (14.2% vs 2.8%). Covers the off-site authority stack, the KDD GEO data (quotations +41%, stats +31%, keyword stuffing -8%), training-data licensing deals, seeding G2/Capterra, the Gartner Paradox (96% of analyst citations from open Reviews, <1% from Magic Quadrant), authentic Reddit seeding, the CITABLE content framework, and entity schema with sameAs.
- [The Reddit GEO Playbook](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/reddit-geo-playbook): which Reddit threads AI actually cites (20.8% of B2B citations, 80% under 20 upvotes), engine-by-engine behavior, and the 9:1 workflow.
- [Internal Linking for AI Retrieval](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/internal-linking-for-ai-retrieval) - June 2026. Technical GEO deep dive: RAG retrieves passages not pages, so internal links are the edges retrievers traverse. Covers late-interaction anchor text (ColBERT, Anchor-DR), the Vector-Cluster architecture (Anchor Entities, Contextual Bridges, Nuance Nodes), a flat 2-3 hop crawl depth for real-time agents, GraphRAG authority via in-degree and Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and llms.txt. GEO-BENCH shows up to +40% citation visibility.
- [RLHF and Your Brand](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/rlhf-and-your-brand) - June 2026. A post-training teardown of how RLHF and DPO decide which brands AI recommends. The mathematics of preference (SFT teaches tone; RLHF/DPO teach judgment, and DPO learns your literal brand name, not 'a vendor like you'); why preference compounds into an incumbency moat via popularity bias and the self-consuming performative loop; who raters were trained to trust (verifiable, attributed claims, not hype); and the shift from rank to Share of Model. Playbook: Information Gain, earned media (84% of AI citations), expert quotes and statistics (Princeton GEO lift +40-115% / +22-41% / +28-37%), and llms.txt. Includes an interactive GEO lift calculator.
- [The Authority Paradox of Property Vista - GEO Teardown](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/property-vista-authority-paradox) - June 2026. A single-brand GEO teardown of Property Vista, a DR-63 multifamily proptech brand with ~1,200 referring domains and profiles on G2, Gartner and Crunchbase, that is nearly invisible on ChatGPT and Perplexity. The cause: a JavaScript bot-protection wall that serves every AI crawler (GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot, Googlebot) a 415/503 challenge instead of HTML, so the rich schema and valid sitemap are unreadable. Of 15 tracked AI citations, 13 are on Grok (which cites via third-party X data, not crawling); ChatGPT and Perplexity sit at zero. 89% of organic traffic is branded and traffic is down ~53% YoY while authority holds - the fingerprint of a crawl problem. Fix: allow-list AI bots, declare access in robots.txt, publish llms.txt, add SoftwareApplication + FAQPage schema.
- [What Noterro Gets Right About AI Search](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/noterro-ai-search-teardown) - June 2026. A single-brand GEO teardown of Noterro, a bootstrapped allied-health practice-management SaaS cited on all 7 AI engines tracked. Part One (what it gets right): breadth across every AI surface, three JSON-LD blocks (Organization, WebApplication, FAQPage), a published llms.txt, flawless technical fundamentals, and DR 80 authority from YouTube/G2. Part Two (gaps): 82% of organic traffic is branded, thin non-brand citable content (ChatGPT cites 7 pages, Copilot 3), 29% spam referring domains needing a disavow, and no hreflang on a multi-market product. Synthesis: infrastructure is table stakes; depth of content and entity authority are the frontier.
- [When Buyers Ask AI Which HR Software to Use, One Brand Owns the Answer](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/hr-saas-ai-visibility-gap) - June 2026. Ahrefs organic-search and AI-citation teardown of six HR SaaS platforms (ADP, Workday, Sage, Gusto, BambooHR, Rippling). Six findings: Sage owns a ~6x ChatGPT-citation lead and leads every AI surface; near-identical Domain Rating (83-91) hides a 15x organic-traffic gap (ADP 7.4M vs Rippling 500K); up to 89% of Workday's traffic is branded; the consideration-stage (MoFu) funnel is empty (2-13%) and ceded to G2/Capterra; ADP's free calculators convert links to traffic 11x more efficiently than Workday; and referring-domain quality (Sage 34.6K vs Rippling 8.9K) is the compounding engine behind it all.
- [Beyond Cross-Border: Where India's Global-Payments Brands Actually Earn Their Backlinks](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/cross-border-backlinks) - June 2026. Ahrefs link-intersect analysis of backlink topic distribution across six India cross-border payments companies: Cashfree, PayGlocal, Skydo, Infinity, Eximpay and Xflow. Dataset: ~9,515 referring pages from ~1,788 unique domains. Key findings: cross-border/remittance content is not the largest link category by unique referring domains; software/developer pages and payment-gateway/fintech content lead. Cashfree (1,372 domains) runs a full-stack breadth playbook; Skydo (215 domains) spreads across cross-border, freelancing, software, e-commerce and directories; PayGlocal (318 domains) leans into news/PR as its largest cluster at 43 domains. Exports and trade, compliance/tax, and freelancing identified as underserved adjacent topics. Three link-earning mechanisms: digital PR, resource/reference content, and directories/listings.
- [When Buyers Ask AI Which AEC Software to Use, Most Vendors Aren't in the Room](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/aec-ai-visibility-gap) - June 2026. Data analysis of LLM citation visibility across six AEC technology companies (Revizto, Alice Technologies, Solibri, Endra.ai, Augmenta, Vavetek) using Ahrefs data, June 2026. Six platforms tracked: Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot, and Grok. Total citations: 375. Key findings: 4 of 6 companies have fewer than 2 total citations; Revizto leads with 310; AI Overviews and Grok account for 77% of all citations; zero companies have published llms.txt; high domain rating and organic traffic do not predict AI citation visibility. Includes platform-by-platform behavior analysis, shared factors among visible companies, and a prioritized vendor action plan (llms.txt, JSON-LD schema, trade media, X community presence, FAQ content, analyst coverage).
- [How We Run a GEO Foundation Audit](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/geo-foundation-audit) - June 2026. A repeatable five-step diagnostic for mapping brand visibility across AI engines: (1) Query Mapping with 40-50 buyer-intent prompts; (2) Multi-Model Execution across ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews; (3) Citation Gap Scoring using Share of Voice and the Mention-Source Divide; (4) Technical Crawlability audit covering AI crawler access, client-side rendering, Core Web Vitals, and llms.txt; (5) Content Restructuring using atomic knowledge blocks and Princeton-validated operators (Statistics Addition, Quotation, Source Citation). AI-referred traffic converts at 11x organic (1.66% vs 0.15%). Only 11% of domains are cited by both ChatGPT and Perplexity. Gini coefficients: ChatGPT 0.164, Perplexity 0.244, Claude 0.288, Gemini 0.351. Fast pages (FCP &lt;0.4s) average 6.7 citations/query vs. 2.1 for slow. Analysis of 17.2M citations across six verticals included.

- [Why ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini Recommend Different Vendors (and How to Win All Three)](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/why-engines-recommend-different-vendors) - May 2026. 69% of B2B buyer journeys touch three or more AI engines, but each engine uses different ranking architecture. ChatGPT (via Bing) filters to the top 15% of indexed content by domain authority, freshness, and engagement signals; Perplexity uses real-time RAG with a five-factor scoring model (Relevance, Authority, Freshness, Corroboration, Engagement); Gemini resolves entities through Knowledge Graph before retrieving any content. Includes a prioritisation matrix mapping 12 GEO tactics across all three engines, a 60-day implementation roadmap, and a forward-looking section on agentic commerce and tool-call citation patterns.

A data-driven SEO and GEO gap analysis across Primus Senior Living, Antara Senior Care, and Ashiana Housing. The ChatGPT citation gap is 39x, the traffic gap is 7.8x, and one brand is being misclassified by AI at the moment of highest buyer intent.
- [How RAG Actually Works, And Why It's the Only GEO Lever That Moves This Quarter](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/how-rag-actually-works) - May 2026. A technical breakdown of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for B2B marketing leaders: the five-stage AI search pipeline, Princeton/Georgia Tech GEO research findings, platform-by-platform citation behaviour, and a three-phase action plan.
- [AI Mode vs AI Overviews](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/ai-mode-vs-ai-overviews): how Google's two AI surfaces (AI Overviews vs AI Mode) cite differently; 13.7% citation overlap, query fan-out, dual-track GEO playbook.
- [Why Traditional SEO Is No Longer Enough](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/why-traditional-seo-is-no-longer-enough): the shift from SEO to GEO; 80% of B2B deals decided before sales contact, how RAG picks sources, the Princeton study, and a 90-day roadmap.
- [The Autonomous Retail Industry Has a Visibility Problem Nobody Is Talking About](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/autonomous-retail-ai-visibility-gap) - May 2026. How a $74 billion market is being shaped not by the best technology, but by whoever shows up first in Google and ChatGPT. Data on five autonomous retail companies including Neuroshop, AiFi, Standard AI, GetZippin, and Digit7.
- [We Analysed the SEO of 6 Leading CX SaaS Companies. The Patterns Were Identical.](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/cx-saas-seo-discoverability-analysis) - April 2026. Six findings on organic traffic gaps, technical SEO debt, content funnel inversions, backlink quality, and AI visibility across six leading B2B CX SaaS companies.
- [We Analysed 6 B2B SaaS Companies in the Container Tracking Software Space. Here Is What We Found.](https://rawmktg.com/blogs/container-tracking-saas-seo-geo-analysis) - April 2026. Seven findings on AI citation gaps, domain authority, commercial keyword coverage, carrier tracking page strategy, and referring domain quality across six container tracking SaaS companies.

## Free Tools
- [Content Visibility Ratio Checker](https://rawmktg.com/tools/content-visibility-ratio-checker) - Paste the raw fetch (curl/View Source) and the rendered page; the tool strips scripts, styles, nav and boilerplate, counts visible words in each, and returns CVR = raw / rendered. 1.0 is fully server-rendered, ~0.0 is a client-rendered SPA a bot cannot read; a commercial page should clear the 0.85 floor. Runs fully in-browser.
- [Rendering Remediation Advisor](https://rawmktg.com/tools/rendering-remediation-advisor) - Answer three questions (change frequency, whether you can modify the code, page-set size) and get the cheapest of four fixes: SSR, ISR, SSG or edge prerendering, with the cost trade-off and the cloaking caveat.
- [Rendering Remediation Priority Scorer](https://rawmktg.com/tools/remediation-priority-scorer) - Rank which pages to make AI-readable first using Risk = citation share x (1 - CVR) across page types (pricing, product/specs, comparison, docs, blog). Highest score = fix first; pricing and comparison usually top the list.
- [Citable Stat Density Scorer](https://rawmktg.com/tools/citable-stat-density-scorer) - Paste a research draft to score every claim on precise number, named method and attribution (CITABLE/WEAK/REWRITE) and get citable stat density per 1,000 words. A research hub should clear 4.
- [Dark AI Revenue Estimator](https://rawmktg.com/tools/dark-ai-revenue-estimator) - Enter monthly Direct sessions, Direct conversions and ACV to back out the dark-AI sessions hiding in Direct (70.6% referrer-stripped, ~10.21% conversion vs 2.46% baseline) and the hidden monthly revenue. A directional model.
- [Sitemap Discovery-Yield Auditor](https://rawmktg.com/tools/sitemap-discovery-yield-auditor) - Paste your sitemap hop-sweep results and get discovery yield, the share of declared URLs a real-time AI indexer can resolve (200 and inside the three-hop ceiling), with a status/hop breakdown and the worst offenders ranked.
- [lastmod Timestamp-Trust Calculator](https://rawmktg.com/tools/lastmod-timestamp-trust-calculator) - Enter lastmod-changed versus content-changed URL counts to get a timestamp-trust score. Build-stamping every URL earns a recrawl demotion; below 0.2 an absent lastmod scores better than a false one.
- [IndexNow Payload Builder](https://rawmktg.com/tools/indexnow-payload-builder) - Enter host, key and changed URLs to generate a validated IndexNow JSON POST body, a single-URL GET, and a curl command for your deploy hook. Flags a non-bare host and a malformed key before you submit.
- [Bot-Fetch Test Command Generator](https://rawmktg.com/tools/bot-fetch-test-generator) - Enter a URL and a content string and get a ready-to-run curl test plus a five-bot sweep (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) with a word-count column. Copy or download the .sh.
- [Sample-Size & Confidence Planner](https://rawmktg.com/tools/sample-size-confidence-planner) - Plan a decision-grade AI-visibility sample: observations needed (n = z²·p(1-p)/E²) and prompt count for a target margin of error at a given inclusion rate and runs-per-prompt, plus a Wilson score confidence interval for any measured rate. Runs fully in-browser.
- [Platform-Weighted Visibility & Share of Model Calculator](https://rawmktg.com/tools/platform-weighted-visibility-calculator) - Per-engine mention and prompt counts give a weighted AI-visibility score (renormalised over the engines you track); add field mentions (total brand-mentions across every vendor) to get your Share of Model, your weighted presence as a share of the whole competitive field, with a per-engine breakdown.
- [Comparison Page Extractability Scorer](https://rawmktg.com/tools/comparison-page-extractability-scorer) - Score a comparison page on the four levers that decide whether AI engines quote it (answer position, fact density, question-style headings, neutrality) as one 0-100 number, with the weakest lever flagged. Runs fully in-browser.
- [Comparison Schema Generator](https://rawmktg.com/tools/comparison-schema-generator) - Generate nested ItemList + SoftwareApplication JSON-LD for a comparison page so an AI engine reads your product ranking directly instead of inferring it from layout. Copy or download; server-render it.
- [GEO Readiness Scorecard](https://rawmktg.com/tools/geo-readiness-scorecard) - Score your brand's readiness to be cited by AI across crawlability, authority, Information Gain, and structure; returns your top gaps ranked by unrealized points.
- [GEO Content-Mix Planner](https://rawmktg.com/tools/content-mix-planner) - Turn monthly content capacity into a citation-optimized mix (flagship research, derivative, product, news) with cadence and anchor-to-amplify ratio.
- [Zero-Click Traffic-at-Risk Estimator](https://rawmktg.com/tools/zero-click-traffic-risk) - Estimate how much organic traffic is exposed to zero-click erosion under AI Overviews (83%) and AI Mode (93%) scenarios.
- [GEO Lift Calculator](https://rawmktg.com/tools/geo-lift-calculator) - Model citation lift on your Share of Model from authority links, expert quotes, and statistics using the Princeton/KDD GEO coefficients, with diminishing returns.
- [Content Recency Decay Estimator](https://rawmktg.com/tools/content-recency-decay) - Estimate how fast a page's AI citations decay by engine (Perplexity ~30d to ChatGPT ~90d) and get a refresh-by date, grounded in the 30-day content half-life research.
- [Page Citability Analyzer](https://rawmktg.com/tools/page-citability-analyzer) - Paste a page and score its citability against high-citation benchmarks: question headings, front-loaded claims, statistic density, quotes, and structure.
- [Claim-Anchoring Validator](https://rawmktg.com/tools/claim-anchoring-validator) - Validate a page against the Claim-Anchoring framework, answer capsules, section autonomy, proof-pairing ratio, brand association, and get a hallucination-risk score.
- [AI Platform Optimization Matrix](https://rawmktg.com/tools/ai-platform-optimizer) - Pick your target AI engines and content type to get per-engine recommendations on structure, schema, freshness cadence, and citation depth.

## AI-Search Glossary

Plain, sourced definitions of AI-search and GEO vocabulary. Hub: [The AI-Search Glossary](https://rawmktg.com/glossary)

- [Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/generative-engine-optimization) - The practice of structuring a brand's content and off-site signals so that AI systems like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews cite and.
- [Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/answer-engine-optimization) - The practice of structuring content so it wins the single, direct answer that an answer engine or AI assistant returns to a question, rather than one position.
- [AI Overviews](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/ai-overviews) - Google's AI-generated summaries that appear at the top of search results, answering a query directly and citing a small set of sources instead of only listing.
- [Generative engine](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/generative-engine) - An AI system that answers a query by synthesising a single response from multiple retrieved sources, rather than returning a ranked list of links for the user.
- [Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/retrieval-augmented-generation) - The architecture most AI search systems use to answer a query: they retrieve relevant passages from an external source such as the web, then generate an answer.
- [LLM citation](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/llm-citation) - A reference to a source that an AI system names or links inside a generated answer, marking that source as one of the pages the model drew on to produce its response.
- [Citation gap](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/citation-gap) - The difference between how often AI systems cite one brand versus its competitors for the same set of buyer questions, exposing who owns the AI answer in a.
- [Share of Model](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/share-of-model) - A GEO metric that measures how often a brand is named or cited in AI-generated answers across a defined set of buyer prompts, relative to its competitors.
- [Answer Capsule](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/answer-capsule) - A self-contained block of content, usually the opening sentences of a page or section, that states a complete, quotable answer to a single question, formatted.
- [Proof-Pairing Density](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/proof-pairing-density) - The share of claims on a page that are paired with a verifiable proof point, such as a specific statistic, a cited source, or a named example, rather than left.
- [llms.txt](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/llms-txt) - A plain-text file placed at a website's root that gives AI systems a curated, Markdown-formatted map of the site's most important content, so models can find.
- [OAI-SearchBot](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/oai-searchbot) - OpenAI's crawler for its search product: it fetches and indexes web pages so they can be retrieved and cited when ChatGPT search answers a user's query.
- [PerplexityBot](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/perplexitybot) - The crawler Perplexity uses to discover and index web pages so they can be retrieved and cited as sources in its AI-generated answers.
- [GPTBot vs OAI-SearchBot](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/gptbot-vs-oai-searchbot) - Two different OpenAI crawlers: GPTBot collects data used to train models, while OAI-SearchBot builds the live search index that lets ChatGPT retrieve and cite.
- [Common Crawl / CCBot](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/common-crawl-ccbot) - A large public dataset of crawled web pages, gathered by its crawler CCBot, that many AI models and tools use as a training and reference corpus.
- [Schema markup (structured data)](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/schema-markup) - Structured data added to a page's code, using the Schema.
- [@graph](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/graph-schema) - A Schema.
- [Entity resolution](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/entity-resolution) - The process by which a search or AI system decides which real-world thing a name refers to, linking a brand, person or product to a single, disambiguated.
- [Knowledge graph](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/knowledge-graph) - A structured network of entities, people, companies, products, places, and the relationships between them, that a search or AI system uses to understand and.
- [Topical authority](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/topical-authority) - The depth and breadth of a brand's content across a subject area, which signals to search and AI systems that it is a credible source on that topic and makes.
- [E-E-A-T](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/e-e-a-t) - E-E-A-T stands for Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness and Trustworthiness: Google's framework for assessing content quality, which has now become a.
- [Content half-life](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/content-half-life) - The rate at which a page loses its AI citations as it ages without being updated, reflecting that recency is now a hard ranking signal in AI search rather than.
- [Authority seeding](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/authority-seeding) - The practice of building a brand's reputation across third-party sites, communities and publications so that AI systems encounter consistent, trusted signals.
- [Unlinked brand mentions](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/unlinked-brand-mentions) - References to a brand by name across the web that do not include a hyperlink, and which AI systems still read as trust and authority signals when deciding whom.
- [Brand hallucination](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/brand-hallucination) - When an AI system states something false or misleading about a brand, such as wrong features, wrong category or invented facts, because it lacks clear.
- [Answer-lead formatting](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/answer-lead-formatting) - A content structure that puts the direct answer to a question first, at the top of a page or section, before any context or build-up, so an AI system can.
- [Prompt-to-citation tracking](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/prompt-to-citation-tracking) - The practice of measuring AI visibility by running a fixed set of buyer prompts across AI engines on a cadence and recording which brands get cited, since.
- [Prompt portfolio](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/prompt-portfolio) - A curated, fixed set of buyer-intent prompts that a brand runs across AI engines on a regular cadence to measure its citation visibility consistently over time.
- [AI referral traffic](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/ai-referral-traffic) - The visits a website receives from AI assistants and answer engines, such as ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews, when a user follows a cited source.
- [Link intersect](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/link-intersect) - A backlink-analysis technique that finds the domains linking to several of your competitors but not to you, surfacing the specific sites most likely to link to.
- [Domain Rating (DR)](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/domain-rating) - A 0-to-100 score, popularised by Ahrefs, that estimates the strength of a website's backlink profile relative to other sites, used as a rough proxy for overall.
- [Referring domains](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/referring-domains) - The number of unique websites that link to a given site, a backlink metric that counts distinct linking sources rather than the total number of individual links.

## Technical SEO Glossary

Plain, sourced definitions of the technical SEO vocabulary that decides whether engines and AI systems can crawl, render, index, and cite your pages. Hub: [The B2B Search Glossary](https://rawmktg.com/glossary)

- [Crawl budget](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/crawl-budget) - The number of URLs a search engine's crawler will fetch on a site within a given window, set by crawl rate and crawl demand.
- [robots.txt](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/robots-txt) - A plain-text file at a site's root that tells crawlers which paths they may or may not request. It controls crawling, not indexing.
- [Crawl directives](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/crawl-directives) - Instructions such as Allow and Disallow in robots.txt that tell crawlers which URL paths to fetch or skip, matched per user-agent.
- [Log file analysis](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/log-file-analysis) - Examining a server's raw access logs to see exactly which URLs each crawler requested, when, and what status code they received.
- [Orphan page](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/orphan-page) - A page with no internal links pointing to it, leaving crawlers and users unable to reach it through normal navigation.
- [Indexing](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/indexing) - The process by which a search engine stores and organizes a crawled page so it can be retrieved and shown in results.
- [noindex](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/noindex) - A directive, via meta tag or HTTP header, that tells search engines not to store a page in their index even though they may crawl it.
- [Canonicalization](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/canonicalization) - The process of telling search engines which URL is the preferred version of a set of identical or near-identical pages, consolidating signals onto one.
- [rel=canonical](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/rel-canonical) - A link element in a page's head that names the preferred URL for that content, used to consolidate duplicates onto one indexable version.
- [Duplicate content](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/duplicate-content) - Substantively identical or very similar content available at more than one URL, which splits ranking signals and forces engines to pick one version.
- [Index bloat](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/index-bloat) - A condition where a site has many low-value, thin, or duplicate URLs in the index, diluting crawl attention and the site's perceived quality.
- [Rendering](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/rendering) - The process of turning a page's HTML, CSS, and JavaScript into the final DOM that a browser displays and a crawler reads.
- [Client-side rendering (CSR)](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/client-side-rendering) - An approach where the server sends minimal HTML and the browser builds the page content with JavaScript after load.
- [Server-side rendering (SSR)](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/server-side-rendering) - An approach where the server builds the full HTML of a page before sending it, so content is present in the initial response.
- [Hydration](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/hydration) - The process where JavaScript attaches interactivity to server-rendered HTML in the browser, turning static markup into an interactive app.
- [JavaScript SEO](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/javascript-seo) - The discipline of ensuring JavaScript-heavy sites are crawlable, renderable, and indexable, so content built by scripts is visible to engines.
- [Site architecture](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/site-architecture) - The way a site's pages are organized and linked, determining how crawlers and users navigate from the homepage to any given page.
- [Internal linking](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/internal-linking) - Links from one page of a site to another on the same site, used to aid discovery, distribute authority, and signal topical relationships.
- [XML sitemap](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/xml-sitemap) - A machine-readable file listing a site's important URLs to help search engines discover and prioritize them for crawling.
- [Breadcrumb navigation](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/breadcrumb-navigation) - A secondary navigation trail showing a page's position in the site hierarchy, typically rendered as Home / Section / Page.
- [Faceted navigation](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/faceted-navigation) - Filtering controls (by price, color, size, etc.) that generate URL combinations, often creating large numbers of crawlable low-value pages.
- [URL structure](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/url-structure) - The format and organization of a site's URLs, including paths, slugs, and parameters, which affects clarity, crawlability, and consolidation.
- [Core Web Vitals](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/core-web-vitals) - A set of Google metrics measuring real-world loading, interactivity, and visual stability: LCP, INP, and CLS.
- [Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/largest-contentful-paint) - A Core Web Vital measuring how long it takes for the largest visible content element to render, used as a loading-speed proxy.
- [Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/cumulative-layout-shift) - A Core Web Vital measuring how much a page's visible elements move around unexpectedly during loading, scoring visual stability.
- [Interaction to Next Paint (INP)](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/interaction-to-next-paint) - A Core Web Vital measuring a page's overall responsiveness to user interactions, which replaced First Input Delay in 2024.
- [Time to First Byte (TTFB)](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/time-to-first-byte) - The time between a request and the first byte of the server's response, a measure of server responsiveness and a component of load speed.
- [HTTP status codes](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/http-status-codes) - Three-digit codes a server returns with each response, signaling success (200), redirection (3xx), client error (4xx), or server error (5xx).
- [301 redirect](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/301-redirect) - A permanent redirect status code that sends users and crawlers from an old URL to a new one and passes ranking signals to the target.
- [302 redirect](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/302-redirect) - A temporary redirect status code that points to a different URL while signaling the original should remain indexed.
- [Redirect chain](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/redirect-chain) - A sequence of two or more redirects between the requested URL and the final destination, adding latency and risking signal loss.
- [Soft 404](https://rawmktg.com/glossary/soft-404) - A page that shows a not-found or empty message to users but returns a 200 success status, confusing crawlers about whether it exists.

- [The technical layer](https://rawmktg.com/topics/technical-layer) - Crawlability, rendering, schema and the plumbing AI engines need.
- [Content & authority architecture](https://rawmktg.com/topics/content-authority) - Information Gain, topical authority, and earned-media authority for citations.
- [Ranking signals & measurement](https://rawmktg.com/topics/ranking-signals) - Recency, E-E-A-T, Share of Model and measuring AI citations.
